repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6a3ede3576d98ccb45d3c2fde6de699dcc25ab21`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #37444 body and all 6 comments (rulings 7205984444 and, via its citation, 7178954860 on #35212), the PR body, the 3-file net diff against `main` (merge-base `0f8e13b001`), and the 54 check-runs on the head: every one `success` or `skipped`, none failing or pending. One web lookup: nginx's `ngx_http_v2_module` page.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public surface: none changes. The diff is two `content/docs/deployment/*.mdx` pages and one platform-checklist item. No package source, published schema or governed path is touched (Governed Surface Queue Guard: success). **Right.**

**Item `ux-conventions.first-screen-lcp` against ruling 7205984444: encoded, neither wider nor narrower.**
- "on a production build served over HTTPS with HTTP/2" is in the title, in `requires[0]` (`objectstack start`, `NODE_ENV=production`) and in the new `requires[1]` (HTTPS with HTTP/2, deployment front or local TLS front). Right.
- "Each reading names its protocol": step 1 confirms `h2` (DevTools Protocol column or `nextHopProtocol` on the navigation entry, a real Navigation Timing field) and step 5 records it. Right, and the ruling itself puts this in the steps ("whose steps carry the protocol condition"). F1 below is about where the protocol is evidenced.
- "an HTTP/1.1 reading is a control only": step 5 ("never scores a clause") and the new `negative` row. Right. The row also makes a development boot a control. That follows from "production build", so it is not wider.
- `source` cites 7205984444 beside 7178954860. Right.

**Ruling 7178954860's conditions are all kept**: LCP at most 2.5 s, cold cache (step 4, storage reset), signed in (step 2, clause 1), desktop Chrome under the Lighthouse desktop preset (clause 2's `configSettings`, unchanged), median of 5 on home, an object list and a record page (clauses 3–5, unchanged). The "baseline before it gates" condition is met at the new condition by card comment 7204645317 (5 runs per page at `9476092c`), and the revision-2 history row repeats its medians (2297 / 2837 / 2685). Right.

**Revision and history against the checklist README's Change rule** (bump `revision`, append a `history` row saying what changed and why): the bump from 1 to 2 and the appended row are present, the date is consistent with the commit (2026-11-26T23:57Z), and `check:platform-checklist` is green. The row's content has gaps: F2.

**Factual sentences in the two docs pages, each checked:**
- nginx: `http2 on;` appeared in 1.25.1, context `http`/`server` (nginx.org `ngx_http_v2_module`). Before 1.25.1, `listen 443 ssl http2;` was the only form. **Correct.**
- "at most six connections to one origin" over HTTP/1.1: Chrome's per-host limit, and the limit Lighthouse's simulator applies. Correct.
- "about 25 rounds": 150 / 6 = 25, the model card comment 7204645317 describes. Correct as a model.
- "1.4–2 s later over HTTP/1.1": 3689−2297 = 1392, 4788−2837 = 1951, 4309−2685 = 1624 ms (comment 7204645317). Correct. The HTTP/1.1 side is a median of 3 runs (see F2).
- "the gap grows with the round-trip time": follows from rounds × RTT. The RTT-1 ms counterfactual in comment 7193730951 is consistent with it. Acceptable.
- "The runtime itself speaks HTTP/1.1 on `OS_PORT`": `os start` binds `@hono/node-server` plain http. The only TLS listener is `node:https` behind `os serve`/`os dev --cert --key`, and that is HTTP/1.1 too. Correct.
- Go-live line in production-readiness: consistent with the section, and the anchor `#serve-http2-to-browsers` resolves (Check Documentation Links: success).
- "Caddy and most cloud load balancers serve HTTP/2 over TLS by default": true of Caddy, AWS ALB and GCP HTTPS LB. "most" hedges the exceptions. Acceptable.
- `--disable-http2` and `--ignore-certificate-errors` are real Chrome switches. `os user set-password` exists, and a non-development server refuses the dev seed credential (`packages/cli/src/commands/user/set-password.ts` header). Correct.

### ② Semver level

Publishes nothing. No file under any package, so `skip-changeset` is right (Check Changeset: success). `Clause-②: no` on the PR body is right: no accept-set changes.

Clause-②: no

Boundary note for the seat: on this tree the diff touches none of the four L2 faces (no `Clause-②: yes`, no narrowing, no published schema, no governed path). So this record is the review the seat asked for at `TIER_DEFAULT`, not one a face owes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag "L2 owed (not self-reviewed); no governed path": answered above (no governed path, confirmed by the queue guard).
- Dev acceptance notes (~150 figure, 1.4–2 s arithmetic, nginx syntax): each verified in ①.
- `open_questions`: none raised.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): not applicable. No code, no query, no id materialisation.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no external-author note is needed.

**Findings**

- **F1 · should-fix · no acceptance clause evidences the protocol.** The ruling's condition is that each reading names its protocol and an HTTP/1.1 reading never scores. In the item, the protocol lives only in steps 1 and 5. Clause 2's `verify`/`evidence` (configSettings, Lighthouse and Chrome versions) and clauses 3–5's evidence do not include it, so a clause-graded run record can pass clauses 3–5 with nothing in its evidence showing `h2`. Fix: add the protocol to clause 2 (or a clause of its own). For example, verify that `audits['network-requests'].details.items[*].protocol` reads `h2` for the page's script requests in each scored report, and record it, with the navigation entry's `nextHopProtocol`, in the evidence. The Lighthouse JSON then proves the condition offline.
- **F2 · should-fix · the revision-2 history row is incomplete and its control numbers are unmarked.**
  - Its parenthetical "(new requires entry, steps 1 and 5, a negative row, title)" leaves out three edits the revision makes: the rewritten persona, the rewritten `requires[0]` (showcase dev boot changed to a production boot), and the new `source` row.
  - "the HTTP/1.1 control through the same front 3689 / 4788 / 4309 ms" are medians of **3** runs. They sit next to 5-run medians in an item whose rule is 5 runs, with no pointer to the per-run values.
  - Fix now, before the row is the ledger's permanent account: list every changed field, mark the control as "median of 3", and cite card comment 7204645317 for the runs. Revision 1's row set the bar by listing its runs and environment.
- **N1 · nit · HTTP/3 has no classification in the item.** `requires[1]` invites "a deployment's own TLS front", and the docs page itself says Caddy fronts commonly offer h3. Step 1 then demands `h2`, and the negative row names only HTTP/1.1, so an `h3` reading is neither scored nor a control. The item is exact to the ruling (HTTP/2). One clause would close the gap, e.g. "an h3 reading is not this item's reading; re-run with `--disable-quic`".
- **N2 · nit · the persona's reason does not match its account.** It says "an account signed up through the Console whose password is set with `os user set-password`: a production server refuses the dev seed password". The refusal concerns the seeded dev credential, not a freshly signed-up account. The reading in card comment 7193730951 signed up over REST, not through the Console. Either name resetting the seeded admin with `os user set-password`, or drop the reset for a signed-up account.
- **N3 · nit · docs overstatements and one usability gap.**
  - "over HTTP/2 they share one connection and arrive together" overstates: bandwidth still serialises them.
  - "A Console page loads about 150 script files" generalises the object-list figure. Comment 7193730951 counts 120 eager chunks on every page.
  - Chrome hides DevTools' Protocol column by default. Say to enable it by right-clicking the column headers.
- **N4 · nit (accepted, no change asked) · the history `ref` cites the card.** It is `#37444`, where the README's anatomy example shows `#PR`. Revision 1 of this item set the same precedent (`#35212`), and the reading in the row was not a verification re-run triggered by this PR's edit, so no RUNNER rule is broken.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-xtck3b-docs`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

F1 and F2 are open should-fix items. The checklist JSON is not a prose face, so a head that closes them needs a delta read by this reviewer before ACCEPT. N1–N3 are optional, and N4 is accepted as is.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6a8d4710bdb2b7c6f35dffde3406eeb755ef65bf`
Local-runs: none

Delta round 2 against record 7206602019 (head `6a3ede3576`). This round read `git diff 6a3ede3576 6a8d4710bd` in full (3 files, +20 −11, one commit), the net diff against `main` again, and the check-runs on the new head: all 53 completed: 31 success, 21 skipped and 1 cancelled. The cancelled run is `PR-body guards`, finished 00:48:49Z; a run of the same name succeeded at 00:49:29Z, after a PR-body edit, so the cancellation is superseded, not red. One web read: Lighthouse's `core/audits/network-requests.js`.

### ① Derived judgments

No accept-set or public-surface change, as before. The delta still touches two docs pages and the one checklist item. **Right.**

**F1: closed.** The new acceptance clause "every scored run was served over HTTP/2" can be scored from what Lighthouse emits. Each `audits['network-requests'].details.items` entry is built with `protocol: record.protocol` and `resourceType: record.resourceType` (Lighthouse `core/audits/network-requests.js`). Chrome reports `h2` / `http/1.1` / `h3` there, and `Script` is the DevTools resource type. So the clause is checked from the saved report, offline, and step 1's `nextHopProtocol` covers the document.

The clause narrows neither ruling. It adds no threshold, page or run count, and it changes none of 7178954860's conditions. It is ruling 7205984444's own condition ("served over HTTPS with HTTP/2 … an HTTP/1.1 reading is a control only") moved from the steps into a scored clause. Treating an `h3` report as a control is inside that ruling's text, which names HTTP/2 only.

**F2: closed.** History row 2 now names every field the revision changes against `main`: title, personas, `requires[0]`, the new `requires[1]`, steps 1 and 5, the new acceptance clause, the new negative row and the new source row. I checked this against the cumulative item diff, and nothing is missing. It marks the HTTP/2 figures as a median of 5 runs and the HTTP/1.1 control as a median of 3. It names the tool and environment and points to #37444 comment 7204645317 for the per-run values, and those values match that comment.

**N1: closed.** Step 1 adds `--disable-quic` (a real Chrome switch) for a front that offers HTTP/3, and the negative row lists an HTTP/3 reading as a control.

**N2: closed.** The persona now reads "the seeded admin with a password set by `os user set-password`, or any account signed up on that server". This agrees with `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/dev-seed-credential.ts`: the seed is dev-only, a non-development server refuses the seed password on any account, and the operator reset is the way out. "Any account signed up" covers a fresh production database that has no seeded admin.

**N3: closed.** I re-checked each changed fact:
- "about 120 on every page, more on a list or record page": comment 7193730951 counts the same 120 eager chunks on every page, plus route-lazy chunks on list and record. Correct.
- "20–25 rounds": 120 / 6 and 150 / 6. Correct.
- "requested at once on one connection, and only bandwidth paces them": acceptable as a model. Import-chain discovery can still add a few waves, and the 1.4–2 s figure, unchanged, is the measured fact.
- "Protocol column … hidden by default: right-click the column headers": correct for Chrome DevTools.
- The production-readiness line now says "well over a hundred" instead of ~150. Consistent.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged. The diff publishes nothing, so `skip-changeset` is right. The PR body keeps `Clause-②: no`, which is right.

Clause-②: no

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags: the PR body's notes are unchanged; F1, F2 and N1–N3 are answered above. `open_questions`: none.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): not applicable. No code.
- PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no external-author note.

**New in this round (both nit, no change asked)**
- **N5 · nit · non-network script entries.** The new clause requires every `Script` entry to read `h2`. A `data:` or `blob:` script would read `data`/`blob` and make every run a control. The card's readings do not say whether any appears, so this is a wording guard only: "every network (`https:`) Script request".
- **N6 · nit · evidence covers less than verify.** The clause verifies every scored report but asks for the per-protocol counts "from one report" per page. Recording the counts for each of the 15 scored reports would make the evidence match the check.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-xtck3b-docs`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

F1 and F2 are closed and no must-fix or should-fix is open. N5 and N6 are nits and can be taken in this PR or left; this is the final L2 round on this PR unless the head moves beyond the prose faces.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 6a8d4710bd · card #37444 · area s2-ux · 2026-11-27T01:07Z

**L1 checklist**
- **Shape and relation.** `l1-face.mjs --pr 37725` flags one item, `all-checks`. The flag is a `PR-body guards` run (140244521574) that was cancelled when the PR body was edited mid-run. The later run of the same name, 140244684342, on this head is `success`. Every other check-run on this head is a success or an expected skip: 31 success, 21 skipped. `mergeable_state` is clean. Three files: the checklist item `ux-conventions.first-screen-lcp` (revision 2), `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` (new section "Serve HTTP/2 to browsers") and one go-live line in `production-readiness.mdx`. `skip-changeset`, nothing publishes.
- **`Part of #37444` is right.** The PR writes the maintainer's amended acceptance (ruling 7205984444: read on a production build over HTTPS with HTTP/2; an HTTP/1.1 reading is a control only) into the item the run is recorded against. It also states in the deployment docs that HTTP/2 is recommended. The card stays open, because list and record pages still miss 2500 ms. It keeps `pm:dispatched`.
- **Contract review at `TIER_DEFAULT`.** 7206602019 PASSed with F1 and F2 open. The delta, 7207007610, on this head PASSes: F1, F2 and N1–N3 are closed, no must-fix, no should-fix. The seat adopts it. Two of the record's findings matter here. The new scored clause, every scored run served over HTTP/2, can be scored from Lighthouse's own `network-requests` entries. It narrows neither 7205984444 nor 7178954860. Nits N5 and N6 go to follow-up card #37746.
- **Docs read sentence by sentence.** I checked both pages' facts against the review: nginx `http2 on;` from 1.25.1, six connections per origin, about 120 scripts per page and 20–25 rounds, and the DevTools Protocol column hidden by default.
- **Governance.** `check-governed-merges.mjs`: not governed. Tier S.

Tier: S. Landing: ready + auto-merge by this stroke.
